svg.title: Retiring a month in one step
svg.desc: An animation in five steps. The game keeps the last three months of match history in the matches table, which has one partition per month of played_on, from matches_2026_01 to matches_2026_04. Each row shows a match id and the day the match was played. When April begins, the retention window slides from January through March to February through April, the first April matches arrive, and January falls out of the window. ALTER TABLE matches DETACH PARTITION matches_2026_01 then moves January out of matches as a whole, and none of its rows is read or written. A count on matches finds 9 rows instead of 12, while the detached table still holds January's 3 matches. COPY archives them, and DROP TABLE removes the table. VACUUM finds no dead rows, while a bulk DELETE would have left all 3 January matches behind as dead rows.
svg.text: Retiring a month in one step
The game keeps three months of match history, and retires the oldest month by removing its partition instead of deleting rows.
The game keeps the last three months of matches. When April begins, the window moves on, and January falls out of it.
DETACH PARTITION takes matches_2026_01 out of matches in one step. Only the catalog changes, so no row is read or written.
Queries on matches now count 9 rows instead of 12. matches_2026_01 is a table of its own, and it still holds January's 3 matches.
Archive the detached table if January's matches are still needed, then drop it. DROP TABLE removes the whole month at once.
No row was deleted, so VACUUM has no dead rows to clean up. A bulk DELETE would have left all 3 January matches behind as dead rows.
